correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=2, the lower link in the one-dimensional K_{m,n} is a discrete set of earlier neighbors. Case analysis of the first opposite-class appearances gives exactly m+n+2mn maximal generating simplices (m+n target stars and 2mn bridge cones). Each mixed-target face is unique to one bridge, so the descending-subset free-face pairings collapse every bridge cone to one edge; each target star then collapses to a tree. The surviving connected graph has 2mn vertices and 4mn-m-n edges, hence 2mn-m-n+1 circles. The symbolic argument covers all parameters. Independent finite order enumeration verified nine pairs, 132624 orders, and 738 elementary collapses.

The accessible 2026 foundational paper treats stars and cycles, including the known K_{2,2} specialization, but not the all-m,n>=2 classification. The closest indexed complete bipartite results compute ordinary Morse-matching complexes, whose homotopy types do not determine this strong subcomplex. No covering theorem was found; possible unindexed equivalences remain a stated residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a full infinite two-parameter homotopy classification beyond published star and cycle cases. Arbitrarily high-dimensional strong-matching simplices collapse to a graph, with a natural doubled-original-edge cycle-rank interpretation. For example, K_{3,3} has thirteen strong-complex circles versus a published ordinary-complex eighty four-spheres, sharply demonstrating the difference between the two theories and supplying an exact structural benchmark.
